article_title: Pathways to Learning: Exploring High School Students' Learning of AI-Powered Educational Robotics
citation: G. McLaughlin, E. Novak, S. Ahmadi, J. Li, Y. Guo, R. Liu, & L. Borgerding. (2026). Pathways to learning: exploring high school students' learning of AI-powered educational robotics. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10651-w
title: Project-based robotics + AI curriculum structured by P3 Task Taxonomy with backward design
description: The curriculum comprised 10 lessons followed by a robotics engineering design challenge, aligned with K-12 CS standards and structured using Barak and Assal's P3 Task Taxonomy: Practice tasks with predefined solutions, Problem Solving tasks allowing multiple approaches, and Project tasks as complex student-driven endeavors. It was developed with backward design, starting from the design challenge and working backward to essential learning objectives.
requirements: mBot robotics kits with the mBlock block-based coding platform including AI/ML extensions
constraints: Sensor-based programming relied on student-written rules rather than data-driven learning, serving as a conceptual foundation for AI
examples: Lesson 8 had students train an image recognition model by collecting datasets, labeling images, and iteratively evaluating model performance
key_sources: G. McLaughlin, E. Novak, S. Ahmadi, J. Li, Y. Guo, R. Liu, & L. Borgerding. (2026). Pathways to learning: exploring high school students' learning of AI-powered educational robotics. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-026-10651-w

article_title: Less Efficient Neural Processing Related to Irregular Sleep and Less Sustained Attention in Toddlers
citation: Hoyniak, C. P., Petersen, I. T., McQuillan, M. E., Staples, A. D., & Bates, J. E. (2015). Less Efficient Neural Processing Related to Irregular Sleep and Less Sustained Attention in Toddlers. Developmental Neuropsychology. https://doi.org/10.1080/87565641.2015.1016162
title: P3 latency as an index of neural efficiency of attentional processing in early childhood
description: This framework holds that the P3 ERP component elicited by target stimuli in Oddball tasks indexes attentional and information processing capacity, with "larger amplitudes and shorter latencies... generally associated with better attentional and information processing capacity." Longer P3 latencies indicate poorer neural efficiency surrounding attentional processes. The article applies this framework to toddlers, using target P3 latency as a neurophysiological index linking irregular sleep to sustained attention capacity.
requirements: ERP recording during an active Oddball task with identifiable target P3 component, typically via parietal electrode clusters identified through spatial PCA
constraints: The article notes the P3 is an index of multiple cognitive processes with multiple neural generators, so few specific interpretations have been consistently supported; in toddlers it is uncertain whether the elicited component reflects the same P3 as in adults
examples: The study elicited a P3-like component from toddlers during an active auditory Oddball task and found longer latencies associated with poorer sustained attention and more irregular sleep
key_sources: Hoyniak, C. P., Petersen, I. T., McQuillan, M. E., Staples, A. D., & Bates, J. E. (2015). Less Efficient Neural Processing Related to Irregular Sleep and Less Sustained Attention in Toddlers. Developmental Neuropsychology. https://doi.org/10.1080/87565641.2015.1016162
